name: Mozambique
summary: The Indian Ocean coast of southern Africa — the Bazaruto and Quirimbas archipelagos, Ilha de Moçambique, Gorongosa's restored wildlife, and a Portuguese-Swahili culture that exists nowhere else.
when: Dry, clear and calm on the coast from April to October.

entries.caption: Two Thousand Kilometres of Coast
entries.description: Reef, dune and island for the whole length of the country, and warm water all year.
entries.subject: a dhow sailing off a Mozambican island at sunrise

entries.caption: Reef and Miombo
entries.description: Coral reef the whole coast, miombo woodland inland, and the Rift's southern end at Gorongosa.
entries.subject: the Gorongosa floodplain in the green season

entries.caption: Gorongosa
entries.description: A park that lost almost everything in the war and has spent twenty years getting it back.
entries.subject: waterbuck on the Gorongosa floodplain

entries.caption: Niassa and Gorongosa
entries.description: Niassa is one of the largest reserves in Africa, and among the least visited anywhere.
entries.subject: a game track through Niassa reserve woodland

entries.caption: Mount Namuli and Gorongosa
entries.description: Namuli at 2,419 metres, and Gorongosa's own mountain with rainforest on top of it.
entries.subject: the granite dome of Mount Namuli rising from farmland

entries.caption: Murchison of the South
entries.description: Waterfalls off the Zambezi escarpment, and the Lugenda's rapids in the far north.
entries.subject: a waterfall off the escarpment in northern Mozambique

entries.caption: The Zambezi and Cahora Bassa
entries.description: The Zambezi's last five hundred kilometres, and the Cahora Bassa lake above them.
entries.subject: the Zambezi river wide in the Mozambican lowlands

entries.caption: Bazaruto and the Quirimbas
entries.description: Dune islands in the south, coral islands in the north, and dhows between them.
entries.subject: the sand dunes and turquoise water of Bazaruto

entries.caption: Coastal Forest
entries.description: The coastal dry forest of the north, and the mangrove that lines most of the delta.
entries.subject: mangrove forest along a northern Mozambique estuary

entries.caption: Dive, Sail, Kayak
entries.description: Manta and whale shark at Tofo, dhow safaris in the Quirimbas, and kayaks in the mangrove.
entries.subject: a diver with a manta ray off Tofo

entries.caption: Portuguese and Swahili
entries.description: Five hundred years of Portuguese on a Swahili coast, and a culture made from both.
entries.subject: the coral-stone lanes of Ilha de Moçambique

entries.caption: Makonde and Makua
entries.description: Makonde carving in the north, and the Makua women's mussiro face paint.
entries.subject: a Makonde carver at work in northern Mozambique

entries.caption: Peri-Peri and Matapa
entries.description: Prawns with peri-peri, and matapa — cassava leaf and coconut — with rice.
entries.subject: grilled prawns with peri-peri at a beach kitchen

entries.caption: Marrabenta and Timbila
entries.description: Marrabenta on the coast, and the Chopi timbila orchestras of Inhambane.
entries.subject: a Chopi timbila orchestra performing

entries.caption: Carving and Basketry
entries.description: Makonde blackwood carving, and the palm basketry of the northern islands.
entries.subject: Makonde blackwood carvings on a workshop bench

entries.caption: Ilha de Moçambique
entries.description: The old capital, on a coral island a kilometre long, with a fort at one end.
entries.subject: the fortress of São Sebastião on Ilha de Moçambique

entries.caption: The Swahili Coast
entries.description: Ibo, Angoche and Sofala — Indian Ocean trading towns older than the Portuguese.
entries.subject: the crumbling colonial buildings of Ibo island

entries.caption: Maputo
entries.description: Wide avenues, a Mediterranean seafront, and the market Eiffel's company built.
entries.subject: the Maputo waterfront and the Indian Ocean

entries.caption: Coral Stone and Colonial
entries.description: Coral rag on the islands, and Portuguese modernism through Maputo and Beira.
entries.subject: a colonial-era building in Maputo with modernist lines

entries.caption: The Beach Market
entries.description: Fish landed and sold on the sand, and the dhow that brought it still on the beach.
entries.subject: fish being sold on the sand beside a dhow

entries.caption: Warm Water All Year
entries.description: Shallow, warm and calm inside the reef — as easy a sea as the continent offers.
entries.subject: children swimming in shallow water inside a reef

entries.caption: Dive and Sail
entries.description: Whale shark season at Tofo, dhow safaris in the Quirimbas, and reef diving throughout.
entries.subject: a dhow under sail between coral islands

entries.caption: Island Lodges
entries.description: A handful of very good island lodges in Bazaruto and the Quirimbas, and little else on them.
entries.subject: an island lodge among palms above a white beach

entries.caption: Gorongosa's Restoration
entries.description: Local employment, local science, and a park brought back from nothing — worth understanding.
entries.subject: a park scientist at work in Gorongosa

entries.caption: Dhow Light
entries.description: Lateen sails at either end of the day, and water that photographs as three colours at once.
entries.subject: dhows silhouetted against a Mozambican sunrise

entries.caption: Ibo Island
entries.description: Silversmiths, a fort, mangrove channels, and about as far from a resort as it gets.
entries.subject: a silversmith working inside the fort on Ibo island

entries.caption: The Coast Nobody Has Ruined Yet
entries.description: Two thousand kilometres of Indian Ocean, and most of it still without a road to it.
entries.subject: an empty Indian Ocean beach with palms behind it
